To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quaternary BaCu(5+x)Q(6) compounds (Q = S, Se) have been synthesized for the first time, and they are isostructural and crystallize in the unique structure type comprising Cu(2+) clusters and Te(4-) dumbbells, and that the BaCu(5,9)SeTe6 compound exhibits outstanding thermoelectric properties with a high Seebeck-coefficient and a low electrical and thermal conductivity.
hot-pressed BaCu5.7Se0.3Te6 and BaCu(6.1)SeTe(4.9) are p-type narrow-band-gap semiconducting materials, exhibiting a high Seebeck effect and a very low thermal conductivity.
the quaternary selenide-teluride BaCu(5)(SeTe)(6) exhibits high thermoelectric performance, with a maximum value of zT = 0.8 near 600 K.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermoelectric performance and crystal structure of the Ba-Cu-S-Te and Ba-Cu-Se-Te systems.
the thermoelectric performance and the structure-property relationship of BaCu(6-x)Q(2-x)Te(3+x) (Q = S, Se).
the thermoelectric performance and crystal structures of two quaternary compounds with unique structures, BaCu(5+x)STe(5-x) (x = 0.6, 0.9) and BaCu5(1+x)SeTe(5-x) with x = 0.4, 0.6.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BaCu(5,9)STe6 is the most promising thermoelectric material among the BaCu5.7Q(0.6-0.7)Te(6) series, with zT values of about 1 at 900 K.
BaCu(5+x)Se(0-x)Te(6+x) is the best thermoelectric system in the Cu-Se-Te system, and that the selenide is superior over the sulfide.
the thermoelectric performance is superior for the BaCu(5+x)SeTe(4+x) materials compared to the BaCu(6-x)Te(4+x)(S, Se) materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the selenide is the better thermoelectric, but it is not as good as Cu(2-x)(Se,Te).
the quaternary BaCu(5+x)STe(7-x) and BaCu(x)SeTe(7-x) chalcogenides with x < 1 are promising materials for thermoelectric power generation.

the thermoelectric performance in terms of zT of the Ba-Cu-Te-S system is comparable to that of the Cu(2-x)-Se and Cu(2-x)(-Se,S) systems, which are among the best p-type thermoelectric materials known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermoelectric performance in this family of compounds is not only governed by the presence of the Cu(2-x)(Se,Te)(3) phase but also by the BaCu(5,6)Q(6) phase.
quaternary chalcopyrite chalcogenides with a low concentration of Cu atoms can be promising thermoelectric materials.
BaCu(5+x)STe(4-x) and BaCu (5+x)SeTe(4-x) (x approximate to 0.2) are good candidates for thermoelectric applications, in spite of their relatively high electrical resistivity.
